newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya reshuffles cabinet, splits departments.
newsitem.headline: Libya reshuffles cabinet, splits departments.

text.p: Libya on Sunday reshuffled its cabinet, splitting the Justice and Public Order Department.

The annual session of the General People's Congress, Libya's equivalent of parliament, confirmed Abdelmajid al-Gu'ud as prime minister, Abdullah Salem al-Badri as energy minister and Omar Mustafa al-Montasser as foreign minister.
The Justice and Public Order Ministry headed by Mohamed al-Higazi was split into two departments.
Higazi remains responsible for public order and Mohamed Belgacem Zwai, former Libyan envoy at the United Nations, becomes justice minister.
The Education, Youth and Sports, Scientific Research and Training Department was split into three departments.
Maatouq Mohamed Maatouq, who previously headed the whole department, becomes minister for training and the labour force.
Ali Chaari was named minister of youth and sports and Mehdi Meftah Mediresh was appointed minister of education and scientific research.

Soliman Mohamed al-Ghomari was appointed minister of health and social security. Mahmud Badi, a non-cabinet minister responsible for supervision of public accounting, has resigned and has been replaced by Nouri Hamad.
After six days of debate, the closing session of the Congress was broadcast live by state-run Libyan television, monitored in Tunis.
